skill.name: Tense that tells the reader when
skill.why: The verb tells the reader whether something is over, happening now or still to come, so the wrong tense sends them to the wrong time.
skill.how: Find the time clue, like yesterday, right now, by the time or next week. Then choose the verb form that matches it.

lines: Verbs carry time. They tell the reader if something is over, happening now or still to come.
Here the clue is 'yesterday'. That's over and done, so I need the past: 'Yesterday I rescued a baby echidna.'
If the clue changes to 'right now', the verb changes too: 'Right now I am feeding a baby echidna.'
And 'tomorrow' hasn't happened yet: 'Tomorrow I will release it.' So I find the clue first, then match the verb.

weDo.text: Last Saturday, our team ___ the grand final.
weDo.hint: Is last Saturday over, happening now or still to come?
weDo.success: Won. Last Saturday is over, so the verb goes in the past.

options.reason: Will win is for the future. Last Saturday is already over.
Is winning means it's happening right now. Last Saturday is in the past.

weDo.text: Look out the window! It ___ right now.
weDo.hint: Find the time clue at the end of the sentence.
weDo.success: Is hailing. 'Right now' means it's happening at this very moment.

options.reason: Hailed is the past, so the hail would already be over. 'Right now' means it's happening this moment.
Will hail is the future, so it hasn't started. 'Right now' means it's happening this moment.

creature.name: Tocktle
creature.blurb: A flatback turtle with a clock face on its shell. Give its verb the right time and the hands tick the right way.

encounters.frame: A Tocktle found a page from Wren's rescue diary.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Rescued. Yesterday is over, so the verb goes in the past.

options.reason: Will rescue is the future. Yesterday has already happened.
Is rescuing means it's happening right now. Yesterday is in the past.

encounters.frame: Mission control is planning tomorrow's launch.
encounters.text: Tomorrow morning, the rocket ___ to the Moon.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Will fly. Tomorrow hasn't happened yet, so the verb looks ahead.

options.reason: Flew is the past. Tomorrow hasn't happened yet.
Has flown means it's already done. Tomorrow hasn't happened yet.

encounters.frame: The Tocktle's shell has three hands: past, now and future. Sort Tully's footy sentences.
encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to when it happens.
encounters.success: The verb tells you when. Cheered is over, is cheering is now, and will cheer is still to come.

items.reason: Cheered is the past, so it already happened.
Is cheering means it's happening right now.
Will cheer looks ahead, so it's still to come.
Kicked is the past, so it already happened.

items.text: Tully is running onto the ground.
items.reason: Is running means it's happening right now.
Will play looks ahead, so it's still to come.

encounters.frame: Mo's party invitation has a verb in the wrong time.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb in the wrong time, then choose one that fits.
encounters.success: Will bake. Next Friday hasn't happened yet, so the verb has to look ahead.

parts.reason: Friday is part of the time clue, and it's fine. Look at the verb.
Cake is what Mo is baking. Look at the verb.

options.reason: Have baked means it's already done. Next Friday hasn't happened yet.
Was baking is the past. Next Friday is still to come.

encounters.frame: Zed is streaming live. Build what he's telling his viewers.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order. Use the verb that fits the time.
encounters.success: Am fighting. 'Right now' means the fight is happening at this very moment.

accept: Right now, I am fighting the final boss!
body.reason: Fought is the past, so the fight would be over. 'Right now' means it's happening at this moment.

encounters.frame: The Tocktle is reading the dolphin sign at the aquarium.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb that tells you something is still to come.
encounters.success: Will perform. Will tells you it hasn't happened yet. The show is at three.

parts.reason: Swam is the past. That already happened this morning.
Are resting is happening right now.

encounters.frame: Gus is filming his experiment and talking to the camera as it happens.
encounters.text: Quick, look! The slime ___ bigger right now.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Is growing. 'Quick, look!' and 'right now' tell you it's happening in front of the camera.

options.reason: Grew is the past, so the growing would be over. 'Right now' means it's still going.
Had grown is for something finished before another past event. 'Right now' means it's happening this moment.

encounters.frame: The band's diary from last week's concert has a gap.
encounters.text: We ___ our first song when the power suddenly went out.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Were playing. The song was still going when the power cut in, and it was all in the past.

options.reason: Will play is the future. 'Went out' tells you this all happened in the past.
Are playing means it's happening right now. 'Went out' tells you this was in the past.

encounters.frame: The space station's log has slipped into the wrong time.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb in the wrong time, then choose one that fits.
encounters.success: Repaired. 'Two hours ago' is finished time, so the verb goes in the past.

parts.reason: Ago is part of the time clue. It tells you this is in the past, so it's fine.
Panel is what the crew fixed. Look at the verb.

options.reason: Are repairing means it's happening right now. 'Two hours ago' is in the past.
Repair is the present, for things that happen now or regularly. 'Two hours ago' is finished time.

encounters.frame: Mo's cooking show has been jumbled. Put it back in time order for the Tocktle.
encounters.prompt: Put the sentences in order from earliest to latest.
encounters.success: Burnt is over, is scraping is happening now, and will serve is still to come.

items: Mo is scraping off the black bits.
Mo will serve it to the judges anyway.
body.reason: Use the verbs. The past comes first, then what is happening now, then what will happen.

encounters.frame: Zed found a note pinned to the door of the haunted house.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb that tells you what is happening these days.
encounters.success: Haunt. The present tells you what they do now, these days.

parts.reason: Lived is the past. It tells you how things used to be.

parts: here for fifty years. Now we

parts.reason: Will visit is the future. It hasn't happened yet (lucky you).

encounters.frame: The robot's voice box is scrambled. Rebuild its warning so it talks about the future.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order. Use the verb that fits the time.
encounters.success: Will run out. 'In five minutes' hasn't happened yet, so the verb looks ahead.

accept: In five minutes, the battery will run out.
body.reason: Ran out is the past. 'In five minutes' hasn't happened yet, so you need a verb that looks ahead.

encounters.frame: Tully is commentating live from the grand final. The siren has just sounded.
encounters.text: And the siren has just gone! The Reef Rays ___ the premiership by two points!
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Have won. The win is complete, and it has only just happened, so it matters right now.

options.reason: Will win looks ahead, but the siren has already gone. The game is over.
Were winning means they were ahead at some point earlier. The siren has gone, so the win is complete.
Are winning means the game is still going. The siren has gone, so it's over.

encounters.frame: Wren's rescue notes, written at the end of a long night.
encounters.text: By the time the vet arrived, Wren ___ the wombat's sore leg.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Had already bandaged. The bandaging was finished before the vet arrived, and both are in the past.

options.reason: Has already bandaged links to right now. 'Arrived' puts this in the past, so you need the earlier past.
Is already bandaging is happening right now. 'Arrived' tells you this is all in the past.
Will have bandaged looks ahead to the future. 'Arrived' tells you this is all in the past.

encounters.frame: Zed's profile page has a verb in the wrong time. The Tocktle's hands are spinning.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb in the wrong time, then choose one that fits.
encounters.success: Streams. 'These days' and 'every Saturday' tell you it's a habit that's still going, so you need the present.

parts.reason: These days is the time clue, and it's fine. It tells you which time the verb needs.
Speedruns is what Zed streams. Look at the verb.

options.reason: Will stream is the future. 'These days' is about now.
Had streamed is for something finished before another past event. 'These days' is about now.
Was streaming is the past. 'These days' means it's still happening.

encounters.frame: The Tocktle's clock has three hands. Sort the lines from today's reef report.
encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to when it happens.
encounters.success: Had dived and scuttled are finished. Were exploring and were sunbaking were in progress. Will turn and is going to leave are still to come.

bins: was in the middle of happening

items.reason: Had already dived tells you the dive was finished.

items.text: The divers were exploring the wreck.
items.reason: Were exploring shows the divers were in the middle of it at a past moment.

items.text: The tide will turn at noon.
items.reason: Will turn looks ahead, so it hasn't happened yet.

items.text: A crab scuttled under a rock.
items.reason: Scuttled is the simple past. It happened and it's over.

items.text: The seals were sunbaking on the rocks.
items.reason: Were sunbaking shows the seals were in the middle of it at a past moment.

items.text: The boat is going to leave soon.
items.reason: Is going to leave looks ahead, so it hasn't happened yet.

encounters.frame: Indi's art show is next week. Build her poster sentence so it talks about the future.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order. Use the verb that fits the time.
encounters.success: Will unveil. Next Friday hasn't happened yet, so the verb has to look ahead.

accept: Next Friday, Indi will unveil her giant mural.
body.reason: Next Friday hasn't happened yet. Unveiled and has unveiled both say it's already done.

encounters.frame: Mo is explaining the kitchen to the crew. One verb shows something was still going on.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb that shows an action was still going on when something else happened.
encounters.success: Was juggling. The juggling was in progress when Dad walked in and interrupted it.

parts.reason: Walked in happened at one moment. It's the thing that interrupted the juggling.
Is tells you how the floor is right now, not what was going on in the past.
Will scrub is the future. Mo hasn't started scrubbing yet.

encounters.frame: A page from a retired astronaut's memoir, on display in the space museum.
encounters.text: When the capsule finally splashed down in the Pacific, we ___ in space for almost two hundred days.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Had been. The two hundred days came before the splashdown, and the splashdown is already in the past.

options.reason: Have been links the past to right now. 'Splashed down' puts the whole story in the past, so you need the earlier past.
Will have been looks into the future. The splashdown already happened.
Are is the present. The memoir is about a trip that is long over.

encounters.frame: Gus's poster about slime moulds has a gap in it.
encounters.text: Scientists ___ slime moulds since the 1800s, and they still find new surprises every year.
encounters.prompt: Which verb fits the time?
encounters.success: Have studied. 'Since the 1800s' stretches from then right up to now, and 'still' tells you the work hasn't stopped.

options.reason: 'Since the 1800s' means from then until now. Studied would cut the story off in the past.
Had studied is for something finished before another past event. 'Still find' tells you the work goes on today.
Will study is the future, but they've already been at it since the 1800s.

encounters.frame: A music magazine interview has a verb that tells the wrong time.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb in the wrong time, then choose one that fits.
encounters.success: Had practised. The practising was finished before she walked on stage, and the whole night is in the past.

parts.reason: Walked is right. She stepped on stage at one moment on that night in the past.

parts: on stage that night, the singer
the chorus a hundred times, so she

parts.reason: Knew is right. It tells you what was true for her on that night.

options.reason: Has practised links to right now, but 'that night' is over. You need the earlier past.
Will practise is the future, but 'that night' already happened.
Is practising means right now. The interview is about one night in the past.

encounters.frame: Wren's rescue report has been shuffled. The verbs will tell you what really happened first.
encounters.prompt: Put the sentences in the order the events happened, earliest first.
encounters.success: Had raided is the earliest past. Found is the plain past that came after it, is patching is happening now, and will fix is still to come.

items: During the night, a fox had raided the henhouse.
Behind the shed, Wren found three frightened chickens.
Right now, she is patching the hole in the fence.
Tomorrow, she will fix the broken gate.
body.reason: Had raided tells you the raid was over before Wren found the chickens. Found is in the past, is patching is happening now, and will fix hasn't happened yet.

encounters.frame: The robot butler is sending a message to its owner. Build it so the timing is clear.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order. Use the verb that fits the time.
encounters.success: Will have cleaned. The cleaning will be finished at a point that is still in the future: when you get home.

tiles: By the time you get home,
accept: By the time you get home, I will have cleaned the whole house.
body.reason: 'By the time you get home' is still in the future. You need a verb that looks ahead to a job that will be finished by then.

encounters.frame: Zed found a diary in the abandoned lighthouse. The Tocktle has gone very quiet.
encounters.prompt: Tap the verb that shows something was finished before the rest of the story began.
encounters.success: Had locked. The past perfect tells you the locking was done before the climb and the creak.

parts: every door before sunset, yet as I

parts.reason: Was climbing shows something in progress in the past, while the door creaked.
Creaked happened at one moment, during the climb.
Am writing is happening now, as the diary is being written.
